Declares NO inventory/hand/range members of its own — hotbar access is entirely inherited from Player/LivingEntity. Relevant client-only members it does add: `public final net.minecraft.client.multiplayer.ClientPacketListener connection;`, `public net.minecraft.client.player.ClientInput input;`, `public void startUsingItem(net.minecraft.world.InteractionHand);`, `public boolean isUsingItem();`, `public void stopUsingItem();`, `public net.minecraft.world.InteractionHand getUsedItemHand();`, `public boolean drop(boolean);`, `public boolean isHandsBusy();`, `public net.minecraft.world.phys.HitResult raycastHitResult(float, net.minecraft.world.entity.Entity);`.

gotchas: Q1 ANSWER: there is NO public `selected` field. javap shows `private int selected;` on Inventory. Pre-26.2 code doing `player.getInventory().selected` or `player.getInventory().selected = n` will not compile. Use `int getSelectedSlot()` / `void setSelectedSlot(int)`.

setSelectedSlot(int) does NOT clamp — it throws. Verified body: `if (!isHotbarSlot(selected)) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid selected slot"); else this.selected = selected;`. Valid range is 0..8 inclusive. It performs no other work: no setChanged(), no timesChanged bump, no packet, no equipment/dirty tracking. Always guard with `Inventory.isHotbarSlot(i)` (or `i >= 0 && i < Inventory.SELECTION_SIZE`) before calling, or you crash the client on a bad index.

Slot changes made from client code DO reach the server without you sending anything, but only via a private path: MultiPlayerGameMode.ensureHasSentCarriedItem() diffs getSelectedSlot() against its cached `carriedIndex` and sends ServerboundSetCarriedItemPacket. It runs from MultiPlayerGameMode.tick() (invoked by Minecraft.tick()) and at the head of continueDestroyBlock / useItemOn / useItem. Consequence for silent-switch code: if you switch slot, act, and switch back within the SAME tick before any of those run, the server never learns about the switch — send `new ServerboundSetCarriedItemPacket(slot)` yourself in that case. There is no public setSelectedSlotAndSync.

Q5 ANSWER: `getBlockInteractionRange()` / `getEntityInteractionRange()` no longer exist. 26.2 names drop the `get`: `public double blockInteractionRange()` and `public double entityInteractionRange()` on Player, both thin wrappers over `getAttributeValue(Holder<Attribute>)`. `getContainerInteractionRange()` (which returns blockInteractionRange()) is the odd one out that keeps a `get` prefix.

Real vanilla range numbers, read from the attribute registrations, not memory: BLOCK_INTERACTION_RANGE = RangedAttribute(default 4.5, min 0.0, max 64.0, syncable); ENTITY_INTERACTION_RANGE = RangedAttribute(default 3.0, min 0.0, max 64.0, syncable). Player.createAttributes() adds BLOCK_INTERACTION_RANGE with no value override (so 4.5) and does NOT add ENTITY_INTERACTION_RANGE at all — that one is inherited from LivingEntity.createLivingAttributes() (so 3.0). Player.DEFAULT_BLOCK_INTERACTION_RANGE = 4.5f and Player.DEFAULT_ENTITY_INTERACTION_RANGE = 3.0f agree.

Creative-mode range bonuses are SERVER-ONLY code: ServerPlayer.updatePlayerAttributes() (private, from ServerPlayer.tick()) applies transient ADD_VALUE modifiers `minecraft:creative_mode_block_range` (+0.5) and `minecraft:creative_mode_entity_range` (+2.0). So the real creative totals are 5.0 block and 5.0 entity — note the block bonus is +0.5, not +1.5 or +2.0. Because both attributes are setSyncable(true), a client LocalPlayer's blockInteractionRange()/entityInteractionRange() reflect these once the attribute sync packet arrives — but you must read them at use time, not cache them across gamemode changes, and client code cannot install these modifiers in a way the server honours.

Player's superclass changed: `Player extends net.minecraft.world.entity.Avatar extends LivingEntity`, and Player now `implements net.minecraft.world.entity.ContainerUser`. Anything that assumed Player's direct superclass is LivingEntity (mixin hierarchy assumptions, `super.` targets, `@Mixin(LivingEntity.class)` overlays expecting Player as the immediate subclass) needs rechecking. Avatar itself declares no createAttributes, no hand accessors, and no interaction-range members.

Q7 ANSWER: InteractionResult is NO LONGER AN ENUM. It is a `sealed interface` permitting the records Success, Fail, Pass, TryEmptyHandInteraction. So `.values()`, `.ordinal()`, `.name()`, `InteractionResult.valueOf(...)`, `switch (result) { case SUCCESS: ... }` on constants, and `EnumMap<InteractionResult, ...>` all break. `==` against the interface constants (SUCCESS, SUCCESS_SERVER, CONSUME, FAIL, PASS, TRY_WITH_EMPTY_HAND) still works since they are singletons; prefer `consumesAction()` or a pattern-matching switch on the record types. CONSUME_PARTIAL is gone. SUCCESS is `Success(SwingSource.CLIENT, ItemContext.DEFAULT)`, SUCCESS_SERVER is `Success(SwingSource.SERVER, ...)`, CONSUME is `Success(SwingSource.NONE, ...)` — i.e. CONSUME `consumesAction()` returns TRUE, only its swing source differs.

InteractionResult.Success.heldItemTransformedTo() is @Nullable (ItemContext.DEFAULT stores null). Also note `heldItemTransformedTo` is overloaded: the no-arg accessor reads it, the one-arg `heldItemTransformedTo(ItemStack)` returns a NEW Success.

InteractionHand is unchanged and still an enum with exactly MAIN_HAND and OFF_HAND, plus `asEquipmentSlot()` and a STREAM_CODEC. getItemInHand(hand) throws IllegalArgumentException for anything else, which only matters if you pass a null-ish/reflectively-obtained value.

There is no Inventory.getOffhandItem() and no public `offhand`/`armor`/`main` NonNullList fields any more — armor, offhand, body and saddle live in a private `EntityEquipment equipment` field. Offhand reads go through `LivingEntity.getOffhandItem()`, `getItemInHand(InteractionHand.OFF_HAND)`, or `inventory.getItem(Inventory.SLOT_OFFHAND /* 40 */)`.

Inventory.getItem(int) silently returns ItemStack.EMPTY for indices >= 36 that are not in EQUIPMENT_SLOT_MAPPING instead of throwing, so a wrong index gives you an empty stack rather than an exception — easy to misread as 'the slot is empty'. Negative indices still throw from the backing NonNullList. And getContainerSize() is 43 (36 + 7 equipment entries), not 36 or 41, so any loop over getContainerSize() will walk into equipment slots.

findSlotMatchingItem(ItemStack) only scans the 36 non-equipment slots and uses ItemStack.isSameItemSameComponents — component-sensitive, so a differently-enchanted/named copy will NOT match. It returns Inventory.NOT_FOUND_INDEX (-1), and can return an index in 9..35 which is NOT a hotbar slot, so you must re-check `Inventory.isHotbarSlot(found)` before feeding it to setSelectedSlot.

Inventory.pickSlot(int) is not a selection helper — it calls setSelectedSlot(getSuitableHotbarSlot()) and then SWAPS the two ItemStacks in the backing list. Calling it client-side desyncs your inventory contents from the server. Use setSelectedSlot for selection only.

Inventory.setSelectedItem(ItemStack) also reads as a selection method but is a content write (`items.set(selected, stack)`, returns the old stack). It is what PlayerEquipment.set(MAINHAND, ...) delegates to.

getMainHandItem() and inventory.getSelectedItem() are literally the same value: PlayerEquipment.get(MAINHAND) returns `player.getInventory().getSelectedItem()`. So writing the selected inventory slot changes the main-hand item and vice versa — there is no separate main-hand storage to keep in sync.

ResourceLocation is `net.minecraft.resources.Identifier` in 26.2 (seen in AttributeInstance.getModifier(Identifier), Player.awardStat(Identifier), and ServerPlayer's `Identifier.withDefaultNamespace(...)` modifier ids). Any attribute-modifier code you port must use Identifier.
Player.HELD_ITEM_SLOT = 499 and CRAFTING_SLOT_OFFSET = 500 / ENDER_SLOT_OFFSET = 200 are creative-container slot ids, not inventory indices — do not use them as hotbar or Container indices.

Server-only Player members you cannot call from client code (they take ServerLevel): `hurtServer(ServerLevel, DamageSource, float)`, `isInvulnerableTo(ServerLevel, DamageSource)`, `actuallyHurt(ServerLevel, DamageSource, float)`, `dropEquipment(ServerLevel)`, `killedEntity(ServerLevel, LivingEntity, DamageSource)`, `getBaseExperienceReward(ServerLevel)`, plus everything on ServerPlayer including updatePlayerAttributes(). The client-visible equivalents for interaction all live on Minecraft.getInstance().gameMode (MultiPlayerGameMode): useItem/useItemOn/interact/attack/startDestroyBlock/releaseUsingItem. Inventory.createInventoryUpdatePacket(int) returns a Clientbound packet and is useless from client code.

Inventory.setChanged() only increments a private `timesChanged` counter (readable via getTimesChanged()); it does not push anything to the server. There is no client-side 'sync my inventory' call — inventory mutation from the client is prediction-only and will be corrected by the server.
